import pandas as pd

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Router with ordered first-match rules.
    Rules are evaluated in order; a row goes to the FIRST matching port only.
    Unmatched rows go to the default port.
    """
    claims = inputs["claims"].copy()
    
    # Initialize output dataframes
    claims_fast_track = pd.DataFrame(columns=["claim_id", "amount", "photos_attached"])
    claims_high_value = pd.DataFrame(columns=["claim_id", "amount", "photos_attached"])
    claims_manual_review = pd.DataFrame(columns=["claim_id", "amount", "photos_attached"])
    
    # Track which rows have been matched
    matched = pd.Series([False] * len(claims), index=claims.index)
    
    # Rule 1: amount <= 500 and photos_attached == 1 → fast_track
    mask1 = (claims["amount"] <= 500) & (claims["photos_attached"] == 1)
    rule1_rows = mask1 & ~matched
    claims_fast_track = pd.concat([claims_fast_track, claims[rule1_rows][["claim_id", "amount", "photos_attached"]]], ignore_index=True)
    matched = matched | mask1
    
    # Rule 2: amount > 10000 → high_value
    mask2 = (claims["amount"] > 10000)
    rule2_rows = mask2 & ~matched
    claims_high_value = pd.concat([claims_high_value, claims[rule2_rows][["claim_id", "amount", "photos_attached"]]], ignore_index=True)
    matched = matched | mask2
    
    # Rule 3: photos_attached == 0 or amount > 500 → manual_review
    mask3 = (claims["photos_attached"] == 0) | (claims["amount"] > 500)
    rule3_rows = mask3 & ~matched
    claims_manual_review = pd.concat([claims_manual_review, claims[rule3_rows][["claim_id", "amount", "photos_attached"]]], ignore_index=True)
    matched = matched | mask3
    
    # Ensure empty dataframes have correct dtypes and structure
    if claims_fast_track.empty:
        claims_fast_track = pd.DataFrame(columns=["claim_id", "amount", "photos_attached"])
    if claims_high_value.empty:
        claims_high_value = pd.DataFrame(columns=["claim_id", "amount", "photos_attached"])
    if claims_manual_review.empty:
        claims_manual_review = pd.DataFrame(columns=["claim_id", "amount", "photos_attached"])
    
    # Reset index to ensure clean output
    claims_fast_track = claims_fast_track.reset_index(drop=True)
    claims_high_value = claims_high_value.reset_index(drop=True)
    claims_manual_review = claims_manual_review.reset_index(drop=True)
    
    return {
        "claims_fast_track": claims_fast_track,
        "claims_high_value": claims_high_value,
        "claims_manual_review": claims_manual_review
    }
